correctness.rationale: The complete 27535-face Cech complex is generated from 30 verified radius-two neighborhoods. A checked sequence of 13495 genuine free simplicial pairs reduces it to 30 vertices, 200 edges and 315 triangles; explicit connectivity plus exact mod-two rank 171 forces rational rank 171 and H2 rank 144 with all other reduced rational homology vanishing. The signed fixed-orbit Lefschetz sum is derived algebraically and checked for all 720 S6 elements; independent stabilized-face traces validate representatives of all 11 classes. Full exact Specht orthogonality and the induced C5 character formula prove the representation claim. The actual included verifier has been executed.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison confirms the strongest same-object earlier theorem [3] determines only a nonequivariant wedge of 144 two-spheres. Neither that statement, the same-graph Rips3 S6 module [4], nor the Kneser Čech2 module [5] entails the new all-class character or induced C5 identification. Actual directed published-finding corpus and primary literature searches found no more general covering statement. Residual risk: accessible/indexed literature cannot prove exhaustive global novelty.
residual_risks: Equivalent equivariant Cech computation may exist in unpublished, unindexed, paywalled or otherwise inaccessible work.
S6 here is the class-preserving subgroup, so claims for the complete 1440-element graph automorphism group are specifically not established.
Research-record search ranking is not a uniqueness oracle; priority is only best-knowledge after identified full-text implication checks.

value.rationale: The intrinsic natural S6 action on a canonical Tutte-Coxeter metric-nerve has previously known Betti rank but unknown character. Its unexpected five-cycle-only support and induction from a nontrivial C5 character distinguish the Cech space from the same-graph Rips representation and prove two naturally defined rationally acyclic quotients. These canonical equivariant invariants are not a routine numerical restatement of the earlier homotopy theorem.
